# What codegraph does, established by installing it

The clarify record named two things that only the work could settle, and both are now observed.
Version 1.6.0, installed globally on 24 September 2026.

**A question about a symbol's callers, in one call.** `codegraph callers state_for` returns six callers
with file and line in 0.10 seconds: two in `harness/cli.py`, one in `harness/measure_criteria.py`, three
in tests. The same answer is available as the `codegraph_explore` MCP tool, which was wired into both
assistants by `codegraph install --target claude,codex --location global`.

**The index refreshes within five seconds of a save, but only while the MCP server runs.** This is the
part the ticket assumed wrongly. There is no standing daemon. With no `codegraph serve --mcp` process,
five saves went unindexed for fifteen seconds each; `codegraph sync` picked them up in 55 milliseconds,
but nothing called it. With the MCP server running, five saves indexed in 0.43, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10 and
0.10 seconds.

So the watcher is a property of the agent session, not of the repository. An assistant with the MCP
server connected has a live index; a shell without one has a stale index until it syncs. That is worth
knowing before the harness routes anything to it: `harness graph` runs as a shell command, and must
sync before it queries rather than trusting the index it finds.

**What the install wrote, outside this repository.** `~/.claude.json` gained a `codegraph` stdio MCP
server, `~/.claude/settings.json` gained `mcp__codegraph__*` to its permission allowlist,
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` each gained a CodeGraph section between marker comments,
and `~/.codex/config.toml` gained `[mcp_servers.codegraph]`. These are the founder's machine-wide
files, not the repository, and they are named here because a tool that edits a user's global
instructions should do so on the record.

**Telemetry was turned off** before indexing anything, with `codegraph telemetry off`. It is on by
default and sends anonymous usage data. This repository will hold a marketplace trade record, and the
default was not worth keeping while the tool reads the whole tree.

**`.codegraph/` ignores itself.** It ships a `.gitignore` that excludes everything but that file, so
the repository's own `.gitignore` needs no entry and doctor has nothing to say about it. The criterion
asking for a gitignore entry is satisfied by the tool rather than by us, which is worth recording
because the next reader will look for the line and not find it.
